h2: Septic & Sewer Sanur – Smells, Blockages & Tank Pumping
intro: If your villa has started drifting a sewage smell into the pool area or drains are backing up after rain, Septic & Sewer Sanur issues almost always trace back to ageing pipework, an overdue pump-out, or salt-air corrosion near the beach. I locate the source, coordinate the tank emptying, and clear the blocked line so you're not chasing it again next week. Send a quick photo on WhatsApp and we'll sort out the rest.

sections.h3: Why Sanur Villas Hit These Problems First
sections.text: Villas here were built 15–20 years ago with original PVC fittings that have gone brittle under constant sun exposure. In Sindhu and Semawang, the salt air accelerates corrosion on pump motors and metal joints well before they'd fail inland. Add brackish well water that clogs filters faster, and small septic tanks designed for lighter use now struggle with daily occupancy. A patch job on cracked pipe rarely holds; replacing the affected section is usually the smarter fix.

sections.h3: The Call-Outs I See Most in These Older Builds
sections.text: A persistent sewer odour creeping through the garden after heavy rain, a toilet that gurgles then refuses to drain, or a grease trap overflowing because nobody cleared it in months—these are the patterns I walk into most often. Narrow pipes in these older constructions mean paper and cooking fat build up fast. I pinpoint the blockage, arrange the vacuum truck for the tank, and flush the line through so it stays open.

sections.h3: What to Send on WhatsApp Before Booking
sections.text: Message me with a short video of the slow drain or the exact spot where the smell hits hardest. If you can snap a photo of your septic tank lid location and any visible pipe joints near the kitchen or bathroom, that narrows things down quickly. Mention whether you run well water or PDAM supply and how long the issue has been building. From those details I'll give you a ballpark range; the final figure depends on what I find on site.

sections.h3: Keeping Your System Honest in Salt-Air Conditions
sections.text: In Mertasari and along the beachfront strips, rinse pump motors and exposed fittings with fresh water every few weeks to slow salt buildup. Avoid pouring cooking oil or thick sauces down the kitchen sink—those coat narrow pipes and solidify within days. Schedule a professional pump-out before the tank reaches capacity rather than waiting for the backup, and check PVC joints near the roofline where UV does its quiet, invisible damage over time.

faq.q: How much does a septic tank pump-out cost in Sanur?
faq.a: It varies depending on tank size, access difficulty, and whether the sewer line also needs clearing. Send photos on WhatsApp and I'll give you a realistic range before anyone shows up at the gate.

faq.q: Why does my villa only smell of sewage after it rains?
faq.a: Rainwater pushes air and gases back through small vent pipes, especially when the tank is nearly full or a pipe joint has cracked from age. It's a common pattern in older Sanur builds and usually points to an overdue emptying or a loose fitting that needs reseating.

faq.q: Do you handle grease traps as part of the same visit?
faq.a: Yes—clearing and de-greasing the kitchen trap fits naturally into the same trip when I'm already on site for a blockage or pump-out. Just mention it in your WhatsApp message so I bring the right equipment and don't make two separate visits.
